transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-01
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Sofia (Ember Head of Search), Derek (Ember ML), Priya (Ember Infra), Alex (Data Scientist)

Summary: quick discovery on embeddings + reranking path, whether Ember will use Redwood Hosted for an initial pilot vs Dedicated/Private for production; heavy focus on vector DB integration, hybrid search (BM25 + vector), throughput and dimensionality trade-offs, and compliance (VPC/KMS).

00:00:00 - Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, ill do a 1-minute intro, im maya with redwood inference and with me is liam, our se. can everyone do quick intros?
00:00:12 - Sofia: yep sofia here, head of search at ember analytics, we own customer search and support search, looking at reranking and semantic recall improvements.
00:00:22 - Derek: derek, ml engineer working on embeddings + ranking models.
00:00:26 - Priya: priya, infra lead, i manage our cloud infra and security requirements.
00:00:30 - Alex: alex, data scientist, focused on evaluation metrics.
00:00:34 - Liam: great thanks, quick agenda: discovery on use-case and constraints, then architecture options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), vector DB integration patterns, throughput/dimensionality Q&A, and next steps.

00:02:05 - Sofia: high level — we have a ~30M doc knowledge base (support articles + product docs). currently using BM25 + some hand-built signals, wants to add embeddings for semantic recall then do reranking. our target is 95%+ relevance lift on top-5 and keep p95 latency under 200ms for search page.
00:02:35 - Maya: ok big picture makes sense; what's your expected QPS for searches and rerank calls?
00:02:42 - Priya: peak is around 120 qps for search front-end, but most queries are batched through our API, we expect ~5k rerank calls per minute during peak campaigns, so throughput matters.
00:02:58 - Alex: for reranking we plan to do two-stage: vector retrieval (top 100) then neural rerank (T5-small or pairwise model) on top 10. cost versus latency tradeoff there.
00:03:20 - Liam: good, that maps to typical patterns. two main integration patterns we recommend: 1) Hosted Redwood for embeddings and model-inference (we host embedding model + reranker) and use an external vector DB like Pinecone/Milvus; or 2) Dedicated/Private where embeddings are created and optionally stored in your VPC vector DB with low-latency connectivity. both support hybrid search.
00:03:52 - Derek: Quick question on dimensionality: we're currently using 1536 dims from [redacted]-style embeddings. are there tradeoffs if we move to 768 or 512? storage/throughput?
00:04:05 - Liam: yes, lower dimensionality reduces vector DB storage and distance compute cost — roughly linear. 1536 offers better semantic fidelity for some tasks; 768 often hits a good cost/quality sweet spot. we can run an eval to quantify for your dataset. also quantization in some vector DBs (like on-disk IVF PQ) reduces memory.
00:04:30 - Sofia: our vendor evals showed small drop in quality at 512 for long product docs, so leaning 768/1536. what's re: hybrid search? we want to combine BM25 with vector to avoid missing exact matches.
00:04:48 - Liam: hybrid is typical: compute BM25 score and vector similarity then a weighted combination; you can do BLEND at retrieval time or re-rank after retrieval. Redwood supports returning embeddings + metadata so you can run your BM25 in parallel and combine scores in your service, or we can recommend rerankers that take both.
00:05:10 - Maya: and to clarify Hosted vs Dedicated: Hosted is fastest time-to-value (we manage models, autoscaling, you call our API). Dedicated gives reserved GPUs and throughput guarantees, predictable latency; Private (VPC/on-prem) is for data residency and compliance — you manage network and keys.
00:05:30 - Priya: on compliance we need SOC2 Type II, SSO/SAML, SCIM, and KMS integration — any redwood docs?
00:05:38 - Maya: yes we'll send SOC2/ISO and SSO docs; KMS/HSM available for Private and Dedicated (for hosted we offer customer-managed keys in some regions).
00:05:48 - Alex: re: benchmarks — can you run a small benchmark with our 100k sample and show p95 for embedding lookup + rerank for hosted vs dedicated? we want numbers to compare cost.
00:06:00 - Liam: yes the SE team can run that. we typically measure throughput (qps), p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec for rerank models, and cost per query. for embeddings-only lookups it's primarily vector DB latency and network; for rerank it’s model latency on top.
00:06:20 - Derek: for vector DB we currently evaluate Pinecone and Milvus; will Redwood integrate with either seamlessly? we have a managed Milvus cluster in our VPC.
00:06:30 - Liam: we see both commonly. integration patterns: 1) host embeddings in your Milvus and call Redwood only for rerank inference; 2) push embeddings to Pinecone and use Redwood Hosted for both embedding generation and rerank; 3) hybrid — generate embeddings in Redwood, push to your DB via API/webhook. For Private deployments we can ship components so inference runs inside your VPC avoiding egress.
00:07:05 - Priya: network-wise, if we use Hosted and push to our VPC milvus, that's extra hops and egress costs. how do teams usually do this?
00:07:15 - Liam: common production pattern is to colocate vector DB in same cloud region and either use Dedicated or Private for low-latency. For Hosted pilots we sometimes sync embeddings periodically to the customer's DB and keep inference in Redwood. We can show a latency heatmap in the benchmark.
00:07:42 - Sofia: on reranking model choice, we need to balance cost and quality. we don't have expensive infra for large T models. any recommended baselines?
00:07:50 - Liam: many start with cross-encoder T5-small or a distilled pairwise reranker — good quality with modest cost. For higher throughput use bi-encoder + lightweight re-ranker for top N. Redwood offers model catalog with performance profiles we can share.
00:08:10 - Maya: also, think about batching and async pipelines. Redwood can batch requests to improve throughput; for low p95 latency you can reduce batch window. for rerank at scale you can autoscale Dedicated pools.
00:08:29 - Derek: curious about quantization and kernel optimization on GPU. we saw other runtimes had token-level variance. does redwood do quantized int8 inference for rerank?
00:08:38 - Liam: for most transformer rerankers we support quantized kernels on Dedicated/Private where hardware allows; Hosted has verified profiles. our runtime picks kernels and quantization based on model and SLOs. we'll provide the model performance matrix.
00:08:55 - Alex: data ops question: do you store embeddings or do we need to? what about retention and PII?
00:09:03 - Maya: policies flexible — for Hosted you can choose not to persist raw inputs; we offer redaction and customer tenancy options. for regulated data most customers use Dedicated/Private so data stays in their VPC and keys. we'll include privacy docs.
00:09:22 - Sofia: timeline — we want a pilot within 2 weeks and production decision in 8-10 weeks, stakeholders include product, infra, legal.
00:09:31 - Maya: Alright we'll aim to get a pilot plan + pricing to you in 3 business days.

00:10:05 - (Discussion shifts to technical architecture)
00:10:12 - Liam: architecture pattern A hosted: Ember calls Redwood embedding API per query (or batch via bulk endpoint), Redwood returns embeddings; Ember stores in DB or uses live retrieval; rerank call to Redwood returns scores. pattern B dedicated: Redwood deploys a dedicated GPU pool for Ember, colocated with your vector DB in the same VPC, private networking; pattern C private on-prem: we install private control plane and inference nodes behind your firewall.
00:11:00 - Priya: if we do Dedicated, what are the SLA and failover — what if we exceed reserved capacity?
00:11:08 - Maya: Dedicated comes with committed throughput and optional bursting; we have auto-fallback to hosted pool in emergencies, with configurable policies. SLAs vary by contract, we'll include sample SLOs.
00:11:25 - Derek: about rerank cost: if we compute embeddings per query versus storing, storing embeddings means storage/DB cost + update pipeline when docs change. do customers usually precompute for docs and generate per-query embeddings for user queries only?
00:11:41 - Liam: yes typically docs are pre-embedded, user queries are embedded on demand. that minimizes embedding compute costs. for streaming user-generated content you might compute and push new embeddings in near real-time.
00:12:00 - Alex: can Redwood host a job to compute embeddings for our 30M corpus?
00:12:05 - Liam: yes we can run an ingestion job as part of the pilot or recommend a worker pipeline. we'll give estimates for compute hours based on dims and model.
00:12:20 - Sofia: about rerank: we want to try a hybrid scoring function of bm25*0.6 + vector*0.4 then re-rank with neural — is that supported?
00:12:30 - Liam: yes that's a standard approach. you can tune weights and we recommend using holdout eval sets. Redwood's eval tooling can track regressions when you change weights or models.
00:12:45 - (Some cross-talk, inaudible)
00:13:10 - Speaker 2: [inaudible] sorry --
00:13:15 - Maya: quick clarity — for the pilot we'll propose two arms: Hosted pilot (fast) and Dedicated pilot (reserve capacity) so you can see difference in p95/cost.
00:13:28 - Priya: security review — for Dedicated/Private we want KMS integration and audit logs, plus ability to rotate keys. also need to review data flow diagrams for legal.
00:13:39 - Maya: we'll attach architecture diagram and security package to the follow-up email.
00:13:50 - Derek: what's the expected throughput for a T5-small reranker on a single GPU? just rough numbers so we can plan capacity.
00:14:00 - Liam: T5-small pairwise reranker doing pairwise scoring of 10 items might be ~150-300 qps per GPU depending on batching and kernel; cross-encoder pairwise scales with pairs so costs multiply. For higher throughput you can shard across GPUs or use a bi-encoder + light re-ranker. we'll provide a performance table.
00:14:28 - Alex: about vector DB metrics: approximate latencies we see from vendors?
00:14:34 - Liam: Pinecone typical p95 for vector-only top100 is 10-40ms depending on region and dataset size; Milvus self-hosted p95 can be 5-50ms depending on indexing (IVF+PQ) and hardware. disk-backed indexes can be higher. that's why dedicated colocation helps.
00:14:57 - Sofia: do you have recommendations for index types for 30M docs?
00:15:03 - Liam: IVF_PQ with HNSW on dense memory for hot shards; shard by tenant or doc type; we can provide recommended configs and cost estimates.

00:16:00 - (Questions about cost modeling)
00:16:05 - Sofia: want rough cost per 1M queries for hosted vs dedicated — do you have ballpark?
00:16:12 - Maya: we'll include pilot pricing but ballpark: hosted compute + embeddings + rerank might be higher per-query but no infra ops; dedicated amortizes GPU cost and is cheaper at scale but requires commit. we'll send example TCO scenarios for your expected QPS.

00:17:10 - Derek: latency SLOs — we need 200ms p95 for end-to-end, is that achievable if we do hosted embeddings + external milvus?
00:17:20 - Liam: it's tight with external DB due to network hops. Hosted embedding + pushing to external DB adds a couple of network roundtrips. For 200ms p95 we recommend dedicated or colocated DB to reduce network. also tune rerank batch sizes.

00:18:00 - (Discussion of evaluation plan)
00:18:05 - Maya: propose pilot plan: 1) Redwood runs ingestion + embed generation for 100k sample and load to your DB or a test DB; 2) we run k qps benchmarks for retrieval and rerank for hosted vs dedicated; 3) we run eval metrics (nDCG@5, MRR, precision@k) and share results; 4) review security.
00:18:28 - Sofia: ok that's good. what do you need from us?
00:18:33 - Liam: we'll need a 100k sample (or a subset if you prefer), access to your milvus test cluster (read/write) or we can host the DB for the benchmark, and a list of queries + gold labels if available.
00:18:48 - Derek: we'll get the dataset and queries. priya will share infra details.
00:18:54 - Priya: also need an SLA on data deletion after benchmark and agreement on ephemeral keys.
00:19:00 - Maya: agreed — we'll include a data handling statement and deletion plan in the follow-up.

00:20:05 - (Short digression on tooling)
00:20:12 - Liam: note — Redwood Console can surface token-level cost, per-route latency, and rollout controls; you can set canary rollouts for reranking model changes. that helps mitigate quality regressions.
00:20:30 - Alex: nice, do you support automated eval alerts?
00:20:34 - Maya: yes, Redwood Optimize supports quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets and evals.

00:21:10 - (Talk about edge cases)
00:21:18 - Derek: what about multi-lingual docs? our product docs are mostly english but support some spanish and french. embedding model choice matters.
00:21:26 - Liam: pick a multilingual embedding model or language-specific models; we'll recommend based on evaluation. multilingual models often trade a little quality per language but reduce operational complexity.

00:22:00 - (Customer asks about contract and procurement)
00:22:05 - Priya: procurement will want a draft contract and PCI / compliance answers. how long to get a security pack?
00:22:12 - Maya: we'll send SOC2 + GDPR + Data processing addendum and a standard security questionnaire within 48 hours.

00:23:30 - (Wrap up and recap)
00:23:35 - Maya: recap: we'll send pilot proposal + pricing + security pack; SE will set up the benchmark plan; you (Ember) to share dataset + infra details; schedule technical deep dive next week. anyone want to add?
00:23:50 - Sofia: that covers it. can we target next Thurs for the deep dive?
00:23:55 - Maya: yes, thursday works. we'll propose times.
00:24:00 - Derek: thanks all.

00:24:10 - (End)
